evidence: "Output one such set"; "all three pairs ... are reacting pairs"; "It is guaranteed that ... at least one such triple exists"
affordance_in_statement: It is guaranteed that the reaction logs contain at least one set of three chemicals that pairwise react. Any such set proves two rooms cannot suffice. Output one such set.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving removal: finding a pairwise-reacting triple is the core task. Rephrasing the guarantee through the laboratory scenario would not change the underlying affordance.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Iterate vertices and pairs of their neighbors, then test whether the neighbor pair is an edge.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Output three integers ... such that all three pairs ... are reacting pairs.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Represent the graph with adjacency bitsets/lists and search for a triangle efficiently while respecting lexicographic order.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: It is guaranteed that ... at least one set of three chemicals that pairwise react.

common_affordance: The statement directly defines the required output as a triangle in an undirected graph and guarantees that one exists.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its submitted search does not reliably satisfy the required lexicographically smallest-triple condition, despite finding triangle candidates.
It relies on exhaustive neighbor-pair enumeration, whose worst-case running time is too large for n=2000 and m=200000, causing TLE.

recommended_edit: No valid single edit can defeat all survivors without changing the core task: any correct solution must recognize and enumerate a pairwise-reacting triple. If a task change is permitted, remove the existence guarantee and add an explicit no-triple output case.
regression_risk: Removing the existence guarantee would also change the required behavior of already-defeated solutions and the output specification.
